title: Invention of the plough
summary: World History Encyclopedia says wooden plows were likely invented in the 4th millennium BCE in Mesopotamia. In northern Europe, cultivation with the cattle-driven ard, a simple plough, is argued to have spread with land clearance from about 3500 BCE. Some scholars suggest plough farming may go back to the early irrigation at Choga Mami, more than 7,000 years ago.

uncertainty.note: Wooden ards date from the fourth millennium BCE in Mesopotamia and across Neolithic Europe, where ard marks and cattle traction pathologies appear by c. 3600–3400 BCE.

where.historical_name: Uruk and southern Mesopotamia, with contemporary adoption of ard cultivation across Neolithic Europe

importance.justification: The plough harnessed animal muscle power to till the soil, multiplying agricultural yields per worker and fundamentally altering human social hierarchy and landscape use.

related.because: Cattle domestication provided the draft animals required for animal-traction tillage.
Plough agriculture produced the extensive grain surpluses and labor specialization essential for state formation.
